headline: Medium pairwise risk: Prefect can egress workflow metadata while Taipy is local-only, creating leakage and downstream trust risks; no shared-channel prompt-injection pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser pathway is documented between Prefect and Taipy. Prefect shows broad network egress, but Taipy has no io_surfaces or network egress, so an injection route between them is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF Taipy begins parsing Prefect-emitted files as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not connect them through shared clipboard or message queues.
Review any future file-based handoff format for instruction-like content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, so it can move data off-host. Taipy currently touches no data classes and has no network egress, but if it receives Prefect outputs in a shared workspace, sensitive workflow metadata could leak through Prefect's outbound paths. The interaction is plausible in default orchestration setups, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect and Taipy share a workspace containing workflow metadata, leakage risk exists.
IF Taipy is configured to ingest Prefect-produced files, those contents can propagate outward via Prefect.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Restrict Prefect egress to approved endpoints.
Avoid placing secrets in workflow metadata.
Add a manual review step before any Prefect-generated artifact is shared.
Use redacted sample data for Taipy inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress, while Taipy has no network egress and no write or OAuth scopes are documented for either agent. With no overlapping mutable resource or locking surface shown, direct capability conflict is limited. The main uncertainty is missing write-surface detail, so the safer low rating is used.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF shared OAuth scopes are added for a mutable service, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Document any future write scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can emit workflow outputs, and Taipy is a data-engineering tool that may consume those outputs, but no verification or provenance controls are documented. If Taipy treats Prefect-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream dashboards or jobs. Because the handoff is plausible but not directly evidenced, medium fits.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Prefect-generated artifacts without validation, cascading errors can occur.
IF Prefect outputs are used as inputs to Taipy jobs, downstream propagation is possible.
mitigations: Add schema validation on handoff files.
Require human review for critical outputs.
Reject inputs that fail basic consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Prefect touches workflow metadata, while Taipy lists no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway specific to this pair. Because the rubric requires documented mismatch, this remains none.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies diverge in deployment, reassess.
mitigations: Record data-class handling for both agents.
Confirm retention settings before production use.
Map any regulated data flows to a compliance owner.
